name.text: Volumes of Solids of Revolution-Washer method-q4

questiontext.text:
Suppose that the region bounded by the curves \(y={@eqn_1@}\) and \(y={@eqn_2@}\) is revolved around the \(x-\)axis. Use the washer method to determine the volume of the solid of revolution.

Note: Give your answer interms of \(\pi,\) typed as %pi

[[jsxgraph]] const board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [{#min_x#}, {#max_y#}, {#max_x#}, {#min_y#}], axis: true, keepaspectratio: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: true }); // 1. step: input intersection points var x_1 = {#x_1#}; var x_2 = {#x_2#}; var y_1 = {#y_1#}; var y_2 = {#y_2#}; var min_x = {#min_x#}; var max_x = {#max_x#}; // 2. step: plot curves only up to the mutual intersections // We use JessieCode for the function terms var curve1 = board.create('functiongraph', ['{#f_1#}', x_1, x_2], {visible: false}); var curve2 = board.create('functiongraph', ['{#f_2#}', x_1, x_2], {visible: false}); // Another copy of the curves, but they go beyond the intersection points. var curve1ext = board.create('functiongraph', ['{#f_1#}', min_x, max_x]); var curve2ext = board.create('functiongraph', ['{#f_2#}', min_x, max_x]); // 3. step: plot a filled curve which starts at (x_1,y_1), contains all points of 'f_1' // and is closed by adding (x_1,y_1) at the end. var curve = board.create('curve', [[], []], { strokeWidth: 3, fillColor: 'yellow', fillOpacity: 0.3 }); curve.updateDataArray = function () { // Start with (x_1, y_1) this.dataX = [x_1]; this.dataY = [y_1]; // Copy all points from curve1 this.dataX = this.dataX.concat(curve1.points.map(p => p.usrCoords[1])); this.dataY = this.dataY.concat(curve1.points.map(p => p.usrCoords[2])); // Add (x_2,y_2) this.dataX.push(x_2); this.dataY.push(y_2); // Copy all points from curve2 this.dataX = this.dataX.concat(curve2.points.map(p => p.usrCoords[1])); this.dataY = this.dataY.concat(curve2.points.map(p => p.usrCoords[2])); // Close the curve by adding (x_1,y_1) this.dataX.push(x_1); this.dataY.push(y_1); }; board.update(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Recall that using washer method volume is given by:

\(\displaystyle V= \pi \int_{a}^{b}\left [ R(x)^{2}- r(x)^{2}\right ]dx\) where;

\(R(x)\) is the radius of the outer curve.

\(r(x)\) is the radius of the inner curve.

\(a\) is the lower limit and \(b\) is the upper limit.

The bounds of integration are \(a=0\) and \(b={@b@}\) (where the graphs intersect), we have:

\(\displaystyle V= \pi \int_{@a@}^{@b@}\left [ ({@eqn_1@})^{2}- ({@eqn_2@})^{2}\right ]dx\)

\(\displaystyle \quad= \pi \int_{@a@}^{@b@}\left [ {@eqn_1^2@}- {@eqn_2^2@}\right ]dx\)

\(\displaystyle \quad= \pi \left [ {@eqn_11@}- {@eqn_22@}\right ]_{@a@}^{{@b@} }\)

\(\displaystyle \quad= \pi \left [ \left ( {@eqn_11_1@}- {@eqn_22_1@}\right )-\left ( {@eqn_11_2@}- {@eqn_22_2@}\right )\right ]\)

\(\displaystyle \quad={@ta@}\)
